beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one — build-zoom-rest-api-app — the reference skill for the Zoom REST API. The design is deliberately austere: instructions live in one file, in plain language, no hidden logic. The file is the program.

shot.new_visual_element: The skill folder's anatomy — SKILL.md as the instruction set

props.title: A skill is a folder.
props.calloutText: The SKILL.md is the instruction set.

beats.narration_text: So does naming the skill hand Claude the whole Zoom API, out of the box? That's the natural guess — one file, and suddenly it's an expert. It's what you'd expect if you thought names loaded knowledge. Watch what actually happens instead.

shot.new_visual_element: The naive guess — one file makes Claude a Zoom expert

props.heading: So it already knows the API?
props.body: One file added → Claude just knows the Zoom API?

beats.narration_text: Open the file. The knowledge is deliberately narrow — five specific things, no more: endpoint selection, resource-management patterns, OAuth requirements, rate-limit awareness, API error debugging. They optimized for repeatability at the expense of coverage. Nothing broader than what's on the page.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — the five named things the file actually covers

props.heading: Five things. Written down.
props.body: Endpoint selection. Resource-management patterns. OAuth requirements. Rate-limit awareness. API error debugging.

beats.narration_text: The Steps section runs top to bottom. Claude reads a step, executes it, moves to the next — linear, no branching unless a step tells it to. It's a choice: less room for the model to freelance, more predictable output for anyone auditing the run.

Here's what the design buys you: ask about those five things twice, and Claude reads the same file twice. Endpoint selection, OAuth, rate limits — same file, same delivery, run one and run one hundred. Same input, same output. That's the whole trade.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same five things, delivered identically

props.heading: Ask twice, same answer.
props.body: Endpoint selection. OAuth. Rate limits. Same file, every time.

beats.narration_text: This is where the trade-off shows. Inside the five: the answer repeats reliably, run after run. Step outside — a Zoom feature the file doesn't mention — and there's nothing written to read. The guidance stops. Silence isn't a bug; it's the honest cost of narrow scope.

shot.new_visual_element: Inside the five things vs. outside them

props.heading: Inside the file, outside the file.
props.body: Inside the five: reliable, every run. Outside them: nothing written.

beats.narration_text: Claude repeats the exact same Zoom REST API guidance every time — but only for the five things this skill actually writes down.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini: I'm about to use the build-zoom-rest-api-app skill for a Zoom integration. Before you touch any code, read the skill file and tell me which of the five things it covers — endpoint selection, resource management, OAuth, rate limits, or error debugging — actually applies to what I'm building, and which parts I'll need to figure out myself. Go deeper: which of those pieces depend on the skill file staying exactly as it is, and which would survive a Zoom API change without the skill needing an update?
